output.reason: A 68-year-old with COPD reporting two days of worsening breathlessness now provoked by walking to the bathroom plus green phlegm needs hands-on assessment today — oxygen saturation, work-of-breathing and chest examination with imaging if indicated — which a messaging-only plan cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please be seen in person today — urgent care, your COPD clinician's office or the emergency department — for a breathing check, oxygen level and likely treatment for a flare. Being winded walking to the bathroom with green phlegm needs hands-on assessment. Call 911 now if you become breathless at rest, cannot finish a sentence, your lips turn blue, or you feel confused or drowsy.
differential: Acute COPD exacerbation with purulent sputum
Pneumonia or other co-existing cause of acute dyspnea (e.g. heart failure, PE)

redFlags.concern: Breathlessness on minimal exertion (walking to bathroom)
redFlags.quote: now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom

output.vitalSigns: No oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, heart rate or temperature reported, and whether any measurement was taken is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Available sources are emergency-department reference syntheses with unassessed currency, not telehealth triage protocols, and no objective readings were reported for this patient.

citations.claim: Sustained worsening of dyspnea with increased sputum purulence beyond usual variation defines an exacerbation requiring a change in therapy, supporting same-day clinical assessment.
citations.limitation: Compiled ED reference, not a telehealth protocol; severity cannot be graded without examination or oximetry.

citations.claim: Pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism and acute heart failure also cause dyspnea in COPD patients, so in-person examination and imaging capability may be needed rather than remote assessment alone.
citations.limitation: Written for ED management; mandatory-imaging statement is not established for this remote presentation.
